summary.overview: Forge wires real build, test, and lint mechanisms, but several enforced gates skip the configured Go lint, package checks, and the license-guarded reference tree, and parts of the always-loaded instruction surface route to paths or tools that do not exist.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: One accurate, loaded AGENTS.md gives strong conventions, but it routes to a deleted directory and leaves the in-tree third-party corpus outside its license guardrail.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Documented startup and diagnostic routes exist and are wired to scripts, while always-loaded instructions mandate tools the project cannot resolve and one tracked corpus clones as empty.

findings.title: CI's only enforced Go static gate is the check the project's own notes describe as failing
findings.reason: The forge-api and beacon CI jobs gate on go build, go vet, and go test only; no workflow invokes golangci-lint even though .golangci.yml, a forge/api/tools.go tool import, and scripts/dev/lint.sh are all wired, and scripts/dev/lint.sh falls back to bare go vet when the tool is absent. AGENTS.md simultaneously documents that go vet ./... in forge/api reports failures from drifted test files. The merge gate therefore either stays red or is routinely ignored, and local make lint gives a different signal than CI. Whether vet fails right now was not executed (no Go toolchain on this machine); the contradiction between the composition and the project's own documented guidance is verified.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add a golangci-lint step to the forge-api and beacon jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml using the existing root .golangci.yml configuration (the tool is already declared in forge/api/tools.go). Then, on a Go-equipped host, run go vet ./... in forge/api, classify each reported failure as test drift or regression, and fix the drifted test files.

## Validation

- cd forge/api && go vet ./... and cd beacon && go vet ./... exit clean, or AGENTS.md names the exact accepted residue
- CI runs golangci-lint on both Go modules and the step result is retained on the run
expectedOutput: Update the existing Workflow owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: The lint agents run skips package changes, and duplicate script trees hide which path is enforced
findings.reason: Makefile, package.json, AGENTS.md, and deploy.yml all wire the categorized scripts/<category>/ copies, while tracked top-level duplicates (scripts/test.sh, lint.sh, format.sh, deploy-prod.sh, diagnose.sh, status.sh, logs.sh) have no referrer and have diverged in behavior — for example scripts/test.sh and scripts/test/test.sh differ in coverage and -race semantics. The active scripts/dev/lint.sh prettier-checks only forge/web/**, and its packages/sdk and packages/shared-types lint branches can never fire because neither package declares a lint script. Editing packages/** therefore returns no formatting or lint feedback from the entrypoint agents trust.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Confirm each unreferenced top-level scripts/*.sh duplicate has no remaining referrer (git grep for its path across Makefile, package.json, and .github/workflows), then delete or fold the differing behavior into the categorized scripts/<category>/ copy that referrers use. Extend scripts/dev/lint.sh so its prettier check also covers packages/**, and remove or satisfy the dead lint-script branches for packages/sdk and packages/shared-types.

## Validation

- bash -n passes on every retained script
- Introduce a deliberate format error in a packages/** file, confirm make lint fails on it, then revert
expectedOutput: Update the existing Script owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: SDK tests are declared but no gate anywhere executes them
findings.reason: packages/sdk declares test (vitest run) and typecheck scripts, but the root package.json routes test and lint to @forge/web only, make test covers Go plus web only, and the CI packages job runs just npm run build:packages. A regression in the shipped SDK can merge with every available signal green. This is a wiring gap verified from script definitions and CI steps; the quality or current pass state of the sdk tests themselves was not assessed.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add steps to the packages job in .github/workflows/ci.yml that run the already-declared checks: npm --workspace @forge/sdk run typecheck and npm --workspace @forge/sdk test. Mirror them in the root package.json test script alongside the existing web test route.

## Validation

- npm --workspace @forge/sdk test executes locally and retains its result
- The CI packages job shows typecheck and test steps for sdk in its run log
expectedOutput: Update the existing Workflow owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: The only agent instruction file routes work to a web/ directory that no longer exists
findings.reason: AGENTS.md lists web as a separate Next.js documentation site and spends a workspace-membership caveat on it, but web/ is absent, git tracks zero files under it, and commit b2e4472 removed the tree inside the review window. Every other path AGENTS.md routes to was verified present, so this is isolated drift rather than general staleness; an agent trusting the layout table for documentation work is sent to a dead directory.

- No doc text still describes web/ as part of the repository

findings.title: The no-copy license guardrail protects an absent path, leaving the in-tree third-party corpus uncovered
findings.reason: AGENTS.md reserves its AGPL/mixed-license never-copy-source prohibition for .reference-repos/, which is gitignored and absent, while the repository actually tracks reference/ — roughly 26 vendored upstream checkouts (coolify, 1panel, pelican, kopia, caddy, and others) with upstream LICENSE files present, never mentioned by AGENTS.md. An agent that reads the guidance and then browses reference/ receives no license constraint for the corpus the rule was written for. No actual copying into Forge code is claimed or observed; the defect is that the guardrail's named target and the real protected surface diverge.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Update the license guardrail in AGENTS.md (the layout row and the pitfalls prohibition) so it names reference/ — the tracked third-party study corpus actually in the tree — with the same study-concepts-only, never-copy-source constraint, and keep any real .reference-repos/ note accurate about its gitignored status.

## Validation

- AGENTS.md's no-copy rule names every third-party corpus directory that exists in the repository
- The rule's stated paths resolve against the current tree
expectedOutput: Update the existing Rule owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: reference/ checkouts clone as empty directories with no declared origin
findings.reason: All 26 entries under reference/ are committed at git mode 160000 (submodule pointers) while no .gitmodules exists at the repository root, so a fresh clone cannot resolve where the study corpus came from, materialize its contents, or check the pinned revisions for drift. Whether the gitlinks are intentional or an artifact of cleanup commits is undetermined; the deterministic metadata state blocks provenance either way.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Decide the ownership of reference/: either add a root .gitmodules declaring URL and path for each retained upstream so git submodule status resolves, or remove the gitlink entries and document reference/ as an externally fetched corpus in AGENTS.md. Confirm the choice with the repository owner before rewriting tracked history-adjacent paths.

## Validation

- git submodule status resolves cleanly for every retained entry, or no mode-160000 entries remain under reference/
- A fresh clone reproduces the documented state
expectedOutput: Update the existing Config owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: Always-loaded RTK instructions tell every agent to prefix all commands with a tool the repo cannot provide
findings.reason: AGENTS.md imports @RTK.md, which ships to every clone and directs agents to prefix every shell command with rtk, to treat RTK-condensed output as the complete result, and to re-run through rtk proxy — while rtk resolves to nothing in this environment and the repository provides no install route or presence check. An agent that follows the instruction gets failing commands or stops trusting verification output; the defect is the unconditional always-safe claim with no fallback decision rule, not a proven failed run, and rtk may exist on some developers' machines.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Make RTK.md's command-prefix rule conditional: instruct agents to check that rtk resolves (for example command -v rtk) once per session and to run commands without the prefix when it does not, and scope the treat-as-complete-result clause to output that was demonstrably condensed by rtk. Confirm with the repository owner whether RTK is a required project tool before instead documenting its install route in AGENTS.md.

## Validation

- A fresh agent following AGENTS.md and RTK.md receives one command-execution rule that behaves correctly whether or not rtk is installed
- The instruction no longer claims the prefix is always safe without a resolution check
expectedOutput: Update the existing Rule owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: Tracked agent rule and workflow instruct running graphify tooling that does not exist in this project
findings.reason: .agents/rules/graphify.md declares trigger: always_on and tells agents to query graphify-out/ through the graphify CLI or query_graph MCP and to run graphify update . after every code edit; .agents/workflows/graphify.md orders agents to follow the graphify skill. The graphify binary and MCP server are absent from the authorized scope (project skills and MCP configuration are zero, and only plugin-owned skills exist), and graphify-out/ has never been generated. Any runtime that honors .agents/ conventions receives commands guaranteed to fail, and the tracked assets contradict the project's configured surface either way; the selected Qoder runtime's loading behavior was not directly observed.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Resolve the intent of the graphify assets with the repository owner: either install and document the graphify tool so the rule's commands resolve, or remove .agents/rules/graphify.md and .agents/workflows/graphify.md together with the orphaned .graphifyignore. Removal touches git-tracked files and needs owner confirmation.

## Validation

- No tracked rule or workflow names a CLI, MCP tool, or skill that is unresolvable in the project's configured surface
expectedOutput: Update the existing Rule owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: scripts/README.md sends testers to commands that no gate reproduces
findings.reason: scripts/README.md documents ./scripts/test/test.sh and ./scripts/test/validate_migrations.sh as the test and validation commands, but neither is referenced by the Makefile, root package.json, or any workflow: CI runs go test and npm test directly, and duplicate-migration validation is enforced through Go tests under CI. An agent that follows the documented route spends turns on a check whose result CI will not reproduce. The underlying gates exist — this is a documentation-routing gap, not a missing validation.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Update scripts/README.md so its Usage section names the enforced entrypoints (make test, make lint, the CI job layout) as the primary routes, and mark any standalone shell script it still lists as optional or developer-convenience with its behavioral difference noted.

## Validation

- Every command presented as the way to test or validate in scripts/README.md has a referrer in the Makefile, package.json, or .github/workflows
